correctness.rationale: Parseval gives the exact seven-term self-convolution formula. Triangle inequality reduces phase optimization to nonnegative moduli. Grouping outer and inner squared masses as \(A\) and \(B\), the inequalities \(a^4+d^4\ge A^2/2\), \(b^4+c^4\ge B^2/2\), \(bc\le B/2\), \(ad\le A/2\), and \(ab+cd\le\sqrt{AB}\) reduce the problem to the one-variable \(h(r)\). Its derivative has sign controlled by \(q(r)=r^3+3r^2-3r-3\), which has a unique positive root \(\rho\). Equality conditions force \(a=d\), \(b=c\), \(b/a=\rho\), and affine-linear phases. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is the exact \(\Lambda(4)\)-type norm and full extremizer classification for the canonical four-term arithmetic progression, the first case beyond the three-character exact classification with several interacting pair-sum collisions. It also shows a structural phenomenon invisible in the phase-only problem: equal moduli are not amplitude-extremal, since \(2.808840\ldots\) exceeds \(2.75\). The constant is a natural benchmark for short-spectrum restriction and additive-relation geometry rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
